There are two examples of American justice that never fail to warm my heart. The first is how O.J. Simpson walked free after a little light murder. The second is how Hims & Hers will undoubtedly walk free after theirs—though in fairness to the Juice, at least he didn't claim to be democratizing justice while brandishing the knife.
There was a time, not so long ago, when a
man who could not perform sexually
might visit his doctor in shame, when a woman losing her hair might accept it as the cruel arithmetic of genetics, when the overweight resigned themselves to the pedestrian tyranny of diet and exercise. These conditions deserve treatment—real treatment, from qualified providers who understand both the science and the human cost of sexual dysfunction, hair loss, and obesity. But then—and you can almost hear the angels singing here—Hims & Hers Health discovered that desperation, properly monetized, could become a billion-dollar enterprise wrapped in the gauzy rhetoric of disruption and accessibility. They were part of a sprawling ecosystem of barely regulated companies that had learned to transform the FDA's good faith into their own profit centers, while maintaining the sort of pious expression one might expect from a Victorian missionary bringing enlightenment to the benighted masses—which, come to think of it, is probably exactly how they see themselves.
We threw in Elizabeth Holmes for a lot less—though one suspects her fatal error was not the fraud itself but the transparency of it, the sheer crudeness of promising blood tests that did not work rather than the more sophisticated approach of selling actual drugs through loopholes so baroque that even their exploitation carries a patina of legitimacy.
The company's Super Bowl commercial in early 2025—titled
"Sick of the System"
—told us everything we needed to know about the particular pathology it represents. There, between the beer ads and the crypto pitches, Hims positioned itself as David against Big Pharma's Goliath, dramatically blaming "Big Pharma's price-gouging" for making effective weight-loss drugs unaffordable while promoting their own cheaper compounded semaglutide as salvation. The irony was not lost on those paying attention—which, given that it was the Super Bowl, was approximately 113 million Americans simultaneously eating nachos and absorbing pharmaceutical propaganda: within weeks, this self-appointed enemy of pharmaceutical greed
would partner with Novo Nordisk,
the very Danish giant behind the thousand-dollar-a-month Wegovy injections they had just finished condemning.
The partnership lasted exactly two months.
Which, in fairness to both parties, is longer than most celebrity marriages and roughly equivalent to the lifespan of a mayfly, though considerably less dignified than either.
What happened in those eight weeks reveals something essential about the kind of company Hims has become. Even as they shook hands with Novo executives in April 2025—presumably in a conference room with aggressively modern furniture—Hims continued selling what their new partner called "illegitimate, knockoff versions" of Wegovy. These were compounded semaglutide injections sourced, according to Novo's investigation, from Chinese suppliers whose quality control standards remained opaque at best and terrifying at worst. Novo Nordisk terminated the deal in June, publicly accusing Hims of "deceptive marketing" and breaking their agreement by failing to halt mass promotion of compounded semaglutide. "We had an agreement that the mass compounding would stop and unfortunately it didn't," a Novo VP
explained
with the kind of corporate understatement that makes one suspect he was restraining himself from more colorful language. "That's why we ended the partnership."
From trash talking Novo while bootlegging its drug, to inking a “strategic partnership,” to getting dumped once the compounding scheme got too brazen: Hims has speedrun the full corporate hypocrisy arc in only six short months. And it’s still only June!

data.title: Define policy forbidding use of AI code generators
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: QEMU项目当前政策拒绝接受包含或 derived from AI生成内容（如ChatGPT、Copilot等）的贡献。由于大型语言模型（LLM）生成的内容在版权和许可状态上不明确，存在法律风险，贡献者无法确保这些内容符合开发者原产证书（DCO）的要求。因此，QEMU要求贡献者避免在提交的补丁中使用AI内容生成工具。该政策不适用于AI在研究API、算法、静态分析或调试等非提交相关用途。该政策可能会随着AI工具和法律环境的发展而调整，但目前违规使用AI的贡献将被拒绝。例外情况需经项目维护者个案审核。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开源软件和自由软件在面对AI生成代码时的版权和法律问题，以及技术实践中的挑战。

不同观点：
• **benlivengood**：认为开源和自由软件在AI生成代码的版权问题上非常脆弱。如果AI生成的代码被视为侵权或公共领域，可能会导致法律纠纷。具体而言，AI生成的代码与人类编辑混合后，可能引发关于后续人类编辑是否构成侵权衍生作品的争议。此外，如果AI生成代码被视为公共领域，则开源项目的许可限制可能不再适用，增加项目被滥用的风险。

• **JonChesterfield**：对AI生成的代码持谨慎态度，不希望评审作者不理解的代码，也不希望合并双方都不理解的代码。相比LLVM的政策更加保守。

• **acedTrex**：指出AI生成的代码打破了传统开源项目依赖的隐性能力标志，提出社会证明等其他方式可能变得更为重要。

• **ants_everywhere**：认为RedHat等大公司关注的是AI生成代码可能包含来自其他项目的版权代码，尤其是涉及闭源和易诉讼公司的代码。

• **abhisek**：质疑如何区分AI生成代码和受未知来源影响的人类编写代码，认为AI生成代码目前只是人类工具，没有独立身份。

• **Havoc**：怀疑一些项目对AI生成代码的反感是否真的出于法律考虑，可能只是不喜欢评审低质量的AI提交。

• **hughw**：希望区分使用AI作为IDE中的超级自动完成功能和高层次指导生成实质性代码的区别，认为应允许使用AI节省劳动力的功能，但避免复制开源代码。

• **wyldfire**：认为拒绝AI生成内容的政策可能是个错误，建议指出AI生成内容可以使用的场景，例如非核心内容的CI设置等。

• **sysmax**：希望根据AI生成部分的大小和范围进行区分，认为小部分AI生成内容可以视为合理使用，类似于视频版权的5秒原则。

• **Aeolun**：认为这些政策无法执行，因为所有编辑器都提供AI辅助代码提示，无法区分代码是否由AI生成。

• **naveed125**：对讨论内容表示赞赏。

• **N1H1L**：使用LLM生成文档，自己编写代码。

• **BurningFrog**：建议包括生成代码的完整提示，以增加透明度。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于AI生成代码的版权归属及其对开源项目的影响。
- 技术社区对如何有效管理和评审AI生成代码存在分歧。
- 一些讨论者关注AI生成代码在实际开发中的应用和效率提升，而另一些则担心其法律和质量问题。

data.title: Ambient Garden
data.author: fipar
data.article_summary: "ambient.garden: an algorithmic audio landscape" 是一个互动式音频体验网站。用户可以通过点击来探索不同的音景，拖动以环顾四周，并随时切换自动导航模式。网站加载完成后，用户可以沉浸在一个由算法生成的花园环境中，享受独特的音频体验。该平台旨在提供一种放松和探索的数字环境。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕生成音乐项目"AmbientGarden"的评价与扩展讨论

不同观点：
• [作者pierrec的观点]
  - 项目是开源的，包括生成音频的代码。
  - 音乐使用纯律（just intonation）生成，最初是因为编码方便，但逐渐深入研究了和声理论。
  - 目前的重点是引入节奏，之前更关注空间中的和声布局，节奏将提升项目的层次。

• [keyle的观点]
  - 对"AmbientGarden"的执行表示赞赏，并提到类似的生成音乐平台https://generative.fm，由Alex Bainter创建。
  - 个人经验是同时播放两个平台的音乐，通过模拟设备增加饱和度，营造愉悦的氛围。

• [LeoPanthera的观点]
  - 联想到2002年和2004年由Mike Oldfield创作的Tres Lunas和Maestro，认为这些作品在当时非常超前。
  - 提供了相关维基百科链接以供参考。

• [yreg的观点]
  - 简单表达了对项目视觉效果（静态天空）的喜爱。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点：目前没有明显的争议，评论大多是积极的反馈和扩展联想。
- 其他值得注意的讨论点：
  - keyle提到了另一个生成音乐平台，并分享了个人如何结合使用这些工具，为讨论增添了实用性的视角。
  - LeoPanthera将项目与历史作品进行对比，提供了文化背景和历史参考，丰富了讨论的深度。

整体来看，评论主要围绕项目的技术实现、与类似平台的比较以及与其他历史作品的关联展开。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对科学项目及相关新闻的评论，包括标题准确性、项目资金问题、技术细节以及对天文数据的疑问。

不同观点：
• [larrymcp] 认为评论中的标题应改为"Earth's"，因为"Earths"意味着多个地球，而原文标题应指单数的地球。这是一个对语言准确性的讨论。

• [UltraSane] 提到了该项目由国家科学基金会资助，但同时指出有1800名国家科学基金会的员工正被住房和城市发展部门驱逐出他们的办公楼。这引入了对科学项目资金和行政管理的关注，并通过提供相关新闻链接来支持其观点。

• [keyle] 对项目每晚生成20TB数据的技术能力表示惊叹，特别是每个图像的处理和下载速度。同时，keyle 期待这些高分辨率图像能够帮助解答一些未解的科学问题，并幽默地补充说“只要答案在南方”。这里表达了对技术成就的赞赏和对科学探索的期待。

• [JKCalhoun] 对文章中提到的200亿个星系和170亿颗恒星的数据提出疑问，质疑可见星系的数量是否可能多于恒星。这是一个对天文数据逻辑一致性的质疑，尽管后续解释中承认星系由恒星组成。

补充讨论：
• [wglb] 提供了一个存档链接，指向纽约时报的文章，可能是为了补充背景信息或验证讨论中的某些事实，但没有进一步的具体评论。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于[UltraSane]提出的项目资金和行政管理问题，涉及到科学项目背后的政治和经济因素，与其他评论的技术性讨论形成对比。
• [JKCalhoun]对天文数据中星系和恒星数量的质疑引发了一些基础天文学概念的讨论。

总体来看，讨论涵盖了从语言准确性、技术成就、项目管理到天文数据逻辑的多方面内容。

data.title: Better Auth, by a self-taught Ethiopian dev, raises $5M from Peak XV, YC
data.author: bundie
data.article_summary: Bereket Engida，一位来自埃塞俄比亚的自学成才的程序员，创建了开源认证工具Better Auth，旨在简化开发者管理用户认证的流程。该工具允许开发者直接在数据库中实现从简单到复杂的认证系统，避免将用户数据存储在第三方服务上，解决了现有工具如Auth0、Firebase等的局限性。Better Auth在发布后迅速获得了大量关注，周下载量超过15万次，GitHub星标数达1.5万，并拥有6000多人的社区。该项目最近获得了由Peak XV、Y Combinator等投资的500万美元种子资金。Better Auth目前免费使用，计划推出付费企业版，同时保持开源社区的特性。Engida在埃塞俄比亚独立开发了该工具，并在Y Combinator加速器中毕业。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Better Auth 作为一个认证框架的定位、技术实现、商业模式以及与其他类似工具的比较。

不同观点：
• [jtms] 认为 Better Auth 的宣传点——让开发者直接在数据库上实现认证系统——其实在过去是很常见的做法，质疑其创新性。他怀疑是否遗漏了某些新的技术趋势。
• [blackhaj7] 对 Better Auth 表示兴奋，但关注其未来的商业化模式，担心风险投资的介入会影响项目的质量。
• [yodon] 持反对意见，认为认证系统的开发非常复杂，普通开发者甚至计算机科学毕业生都未必有能力写出安全的认证系统。他强调黑客在这个领域的经验更丰富，暗示不应轻视认证系统的安全性。

补充讨论：
• [dang] 提供了与 Better Auth 相关的其他讨论链接，显示该工具在开发者社区中已有一定讨论热度，并附上了多个历史讨论帖。
• [dancerofaran] 高度赞赏 Better Auth，称其为“开放源代码的 Clerk”，且没有其他安全方案的负担，暗示其在安全性和易用性上的优势。
• [arend321] 关注 Better Auth 的商业化模式，猜测可能会采用企业 SSO 订阅模式，同时指出其在迁移现有用户上的困难。
• [sebmellen] 将 Better Auth 与 Ory Kratos 进行比较，并询问其未来的收入模式。
• [exiguus] 将 Better Auth 与 Superbase、Keycloak 和自托管方案进行比较，询问其技术优势和差异。
• [yewenjie] 询问 Better Auth 与更基础的认证库 Lucia 的区别，希望了解其功能上的不同。
• [koakuma-chan] 质疑为何一个 JavaScript 认证库需要筹集五百万美元的风险投资，暗示对该项目资金需求的合理性存疑。
• [haneul] 对 Better Auth 的新闻表示喜爱，赞赏 Bereket 的工作。
• [alephnerd] 以幽默的方式提到 Peak XV，并祝贺 Bereket，显示出对 Bereket 成功的认可。
• [abetancort] 提到一个与技术讨论无关的政治观点，偏离了主题。

争议焦点：
• Better Auth 是否真的具有宣传中的创新性，特别是与过去的认证系统实现方式相比。
• 普通开发者是否能够安全地实现认证系统，还是应该依赖更成熟的解决方案。
• Better Auth 的商业化模式及其未来发展方向。
• Better Auth 与其他类似工具（如 Ory Kratos、Keycloak、Superbase、Lucia）的比较和技术优势。

总结：评论中既有对 Better Auth 的赞赏，也有对其创新性、安全性、商业模式的质疑，同时涉及与其他工具的比较。

44380185.article_content:
It’s rare to see a solo founder building a widely adopted developer infrastructure tool. Even more so if the founder happens to be from Africa.
Bereket Engida
, a self-taught programmer from Ethiopia, is quietly building what some developers say is the best authentication tool they’ve ever used.
Engida’s startup,
Better Auth
, offers an open source framework that promises to simplify how developers manage user authentication, and it’s caught the attention of some big name investors. It recently raised about $5 million in seed funding from Peak XV (formerly Sequoia India and Southeast Asia), Y Combinator, P1 Ventures, and Chapter One.
But the most interesting part here isn’t who’s on the startup’s cap table: Engida says he built the entire product back home in Ethiopia before he set foot in the U.S.
Engida told TechCrunch that he started programming at 18 after a friend declined to help him build an e-commerce search app, and he started working on the project himself. He went on to land some remote software jobs and eventually built a web analytics platform that lets developers monitor user behavior on their websites.
But throughout his various jobs, Engida says he kept seeing an issue popping up everywhere: authentication. Every app needs to manage how users sign in and out and reset passwords, and sometimes administrators need to handle permissions and user roles. But he found existing tools were either too limited or too rigid — companies like Auth0, Firebase, and NextAuth offer managed services, but they store user data externally, limit customization, and are expensive at scale.
“I remember needing an organization feature. It’s a very common use case for most SaaS applications, but it wasn’t available from these providers,” Engida told TechCrunch. “So I had to build it from scratch. It took me about two weeks, and I remember thinking, ‘This is crazy; there has to be a better way to solve this.’”
He then scrapped that project and began working on a TypeScript-based authentication framework that would let developers access user data via open source libraries, support common permissions use cases — like teams and roles — out of the box, and scale with plug-ins.

“The idea was that you could add advanced features in just two or three lines of code,” Engida said.
Why developers love it
Over six months working mostly from his bedroom in Ethiopia, Engida built the first version of the library that would go on to become Better Auth. When he posted it to GitHub in September 2024, developers quickly saw the potential.
Since then, Better Auth has clocked 150,000+ weekly downloads, 15,000+ GitHub stars, and a community of over 6,000 Discord members, the startup claims.
Better Auth’s pitch is simple: Let developers implement everything from simple authentication flows to enterprise-grade systems directly on their databases and embed it all on the back end. Unlike hosted services, Better Auth is an open source library that developers can integrate directly into their codebase, keeping all user data on premise, in their database. For companies wary of handing over critical user information to third parties, this feature alone is a major point.
The library has also found unexpected traction among early-stage AI startups, which need to build custom authentication flows that integrate with proprietary APIs, manage tokens securely, and be able to scale without racking up high costs.
“We first heard about the product from numerous startups we’ve worked with,” said Arnav Sahu, partner at Peak XV and former principal at Y Combinator. “Their auth product has seen phenomenal adoption among the next generation of AI startups.”
Better Auth marks Peak XV’s first direct investment in an African founder.
Engida says Better Auth, currently free to use, will focus on improving its core features and launch a paid enterprise infrastructure that plugs into its open source base. This will give developers the flexibility to self-host or opt for Better Auth’s cloud add-ons as needed.
He’s also thinking about how to scale without trading away the product’s community-built feel. On the roadmap, therefore, is hiring a small team to help maintain the codebase, expand documentation, and support enterprise users. For now, though, Engida is still writing most of the code himself.

data.title: Deep Research as a Swim Coach
data.author: suthakamal
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI技术在游泳训练中的应用及其与传统训练方法的比较

不同观点：
• sriram_malhar认为，尽管AI技术在处理PDF和解释截图等方面表现出色，但他对AI能否提供比传统方法（如书籍和Terry Laughlin的视频）更多的新见解持怀疑态度。他认为AI最多可以作为一个优秀的语义索引工具，帮助查找相关信息，但在产生新的洞察力方面并不比传统方法优越。

• netaustin对AI在游泳训练中的潜在应用表示赞赏，并提出AI未来可能通过分析自我教练或远程教练的游泳视频提供指导。他认为，现场教练实时提供的反馈对游泳学习非常宝贵，而AI有可能在未来模拟这种实时反馈的效果。他分享了自己从Terry Laughlin亲自授课中获得的宝贵经验，强调了教练现场指导的重要性。

• suthakamal提出了一个更具实验性的观点，建议通过给一个高级AI提供大量背景信息（如训练日志、个人笔记和游泳教科书的PDF），来打造一个定制化的训练系统。这一观点强调了AI在个性化训练方案设计中的潜力。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于AI是否能够超越传统训练方法，提供新的、有价值的洞察力，以及AI在实时反馈和个性化指导方面的潜力。
• sriram_malhar对AI的实际效果持保留态度，而netaustin和suthakamal则对AI的未来应用持更为乐观和开放的态度。
• netaustin特别提到了现场教练实时反馈的价值，并通过个人经历说明了这一点，对AI能否完全替代人类教练提出了质疑。
• suthakamal的实验性想法展示了对AI个性化能力的前瞻性探索，但尚未提供具体实现方法和效果验证。

data.title: CUDA Ray Tracing 2x Faster Than RTX: My CUDA Ray Tracing Journey
data.author: ibobev
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者如何使用CUDA开发了一个比Vulkan/RTX实现更快（快2倍）的光线追踪渲染器。作者通过深入优化，使CUDA版本在相同硬件上性能显著提升，达到了约105 FPS，而Vulkan/RTX版本为约30-50 FPS。性能差异主要源于RTX硬件加速在处理简单程序化几何体（如球体）时效率不高，而CUDA通过纯计算单元处理BVH遍历，减少了内存流量，从而提升了性能。作者的CUDA实现采用了“内联光线追踪”，避免了硬件光线追踪管线的额外开销。尽管这是一个合成场景，且在实际游戏中RTX核心对三角形几何体的处理更高效，但本文展示了在特定条件下纯计算方法的潜力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GPU计算资源分配在不同模式（CUDA模式与RTX模式）下的表现差异

不同观点：
• [sheepscreek的观点]  
  - 认为在CUDA模式下，程序可能占用了GPU的全部计算能力，因为此时GPU不需要与其他功能共享资源。  
  - 与此相对，在RTX模式下，GPU的计算资源需要被共享，导致性能表现不同。
  
• [E-Reverance的观点]

And this is actually how I learned CUDA.
In this write-up, I'll walk you through the journey: what worked, what didn't, and the key
tricks that made the biggest difference. Whether you're a graphics programmer, a CUDA
enthusiast, or just curious about real-world GPU optimization, I hope you'll find something useful
here.

data.title: Primitive Kolmogorov complexity is computable
data.author: 1ewish
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了Kolmogorov复杂性和Solomonoff归纳的不可计算性，以及如何通过限制在原始递归函数类中来实现可计算的变体。Kolmogorov复杂性指的是在通用图灵机上输出某一对象的最短程序长度，而Solomonoff归纳利用这一原则为假设分配先验概率，从而创建通用预测器。然而，两者因停机问题而不可计算。

原始递归函数是一类重要的可计算函数，它们总是 halt，因此避开了停机问题。这类函数包括大多数常见算法和数学运算。基于此，可以定义可计算的原始Kolmogorov复杂性（PCO），即输出某一对象的最短原始递归程序的长度。类似地，原始Solomonoff归纳只考虑原始递归函数空间。

虽然原始递归函数类不包括某些快速增长的函数（如Ackermann函数），但在实际应用中，尤其是科学和工程领域，原始递归函数已足够应对大多数情况，满足现实世界智能需求。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：
• [catlifeonmars] 认为Kolmogorov复杂性和停机问题描述的是同一概念的不同表述形式，因此说“Kolmogorov复杂性的不可计算性直接源于停机问题”具有误导性，甚至可以反过来说停机问题源于Kolmogorov复杂性。
• [fen11] 指出原始Kolmogorov复杂性（PK）虽然适用广泛，但需要证明其作为复杂性度量的意义。他提到，某些原始递归函数在原始递归编程语言中的实现可能比图灵完全语言中的实现大得多，这使得PK和经典Kolmogorov复杂性可能有很大差异。
• [gerdesj] 批评文章中关于“实用通用智能只需搜索原始递归函数”的观点，认为作者忽略了“智能最终可能需要图灵机全搜索”的可能性。他质疑“实用通用智能”是否真的有用，认为它可能只是一种用于预测下一个标记的系统。

补充讨论：

• 图灵完备性与非图灵完备性语言在表达力和计算效率上的差异是另一个核心讨论点，特别是在AI和智能系统中的应用。
• 对于AI生成的内容，部分评论者（如[4ad]）表示强烈不满，认为其观点浅薄且误导。
• 实际计算中的资源消耗问题也被提及，强调了理论复杂性和实际应用之间的差距。

Kolmogorov complexity
and
Solomonoff's theory of inductive inference
offer formal, theoretical solutions to measuring complexity and forming predictions. However, both are uncomputable, a fact that is often treated as having significant implications in computability theory and artificial intelligence. I'm going to argue that by reformulating these concepts over the class of primitive recursive functions, we arrive at computable and practically relevant analogues: Primitive Kolmogorov complexity (
) and a primitive form of Solomonoff induction.
The uncomputability of
and Solomonoff induction
#
The Kolmogorov complexity of an object

, is the length of the shortest program on a universal Turing machine that outputs the object. Solomonoff induction uses this principle to assign a prior probability to a hypothesis based on its Kolmogorov complexity, creating a universal predictor.
The uncomputability of both arises directly from the
Halting Problem
. To find the shortest program, one must be able to determine if any given program will halt. As this is impossible for all programs,
and
are not calculable.
Primitive recursive functions: a computable subclass
#
The
primitive recursive functions
are a large and powerful subset of the total computable functions. A function is primitive recursive if it can be defined using only basic initial functions (such as the zero function, successor function, and projection functions) and a finite number of applications of composition and primitive recursion.
A key property of this class is that every primitive recursive function is a total function - meaning it is defined for all inputs and is guaranteed to halt. This guarantee sidesteps the Halting Problem. A useful heuristic from complexity theory is that
if a function's time complexity is bounded by a primitive recursive function of its input size, then the function itself is primitive recursive
.
This class includes most functions and common algorithms encountered in computer science. Standard mathematical operations like addition, multiplication, and exponentiation are primitive recursive. Common algorithms whose operations are bounded by the input size - such as bubble sort and insertion sort, or graph algorithms like Dijkstra's - are primitive recursive.
Defining computable complexity and prediction
#
Using this restricted class of functions, we can define computable versions of
and Solomonoff induction:
Primitive Kolmogorov complexity (

The

primitive recursive
program that produces it. The search for this shortest program is now a computable operation, as we only consider programs that are guaranteed to halt.
Primitive Solomonoff induction:
A computable predictor can be formulated by restricting the Solomonoff prior to the space of primitive recursive functions. The predictor would consider only the primitive recursive programs that could generate a given sequence, weighting them according to their length.
The limits of the primitive recursive class
#
The restriction to primitive recursive functions means that certain total computable functions are excluded. The canonical example is the
Ackermann function
, a total computable function whose output grows faster than any primitive recursive function. For even small inputs, its value becomes computationally intractable.
The functions that lie outside the primitive recursive class are those characterized by such hyper-exponential growth. The practical limitations of using
are therefore found in specific domains:
Analysis of Hyper-Operations:
The study of functions that grow at rates exceeding any standard exponential function.
Complex Termination Proofs:
Certain complex programs require non-primitive recursive functions to prove their termination within formal systems like Peano arithmetic.
Worst-Case Analysis of Highly Complex Systems:
Analyzing the absolute theoretical limits of certain algorithms or systems can involve non-primitive recursive complexity.

data.title: IBM's Dmitry Krotov wants to crack the 'physics' of memory
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary:
Dmitry "Dima" Krotov 是 IBM 研究员，致力于通过物理学的数学工具研究生物和数字神经网络的计算。他曾与 AI 先驱 John Hopfield 合作，帮助解释 Hopfield 的单层数字神经网络如何演变为今天的深度网络。他们在普林斯顿大学共同发明了密集关联记忆模型，提升了早期 Hopfield 网络的记忆存储能力。Krotov 现在继续发展 Hopfield 的理念，建立计算模型以改进人工智能，甚至理解智能的本质。

Hopfield 在1982年通过展示一个30节点网络如何存储和检索二进制模式，重新激发了对神经网络的兴趣。他的灵感来自磁性材料，并通过“能量函数”描述系统动态行为，使网络逐步趋向稳定、最低能量状态，完成计算。

尽管关联记忆可能不会取代变压器模型，但它有助于使 AI 更透明和易于理解。Krotov 还通过关联记忆模拟生物计算，帮助解释大脑如何高效处理大量信息。Krotov 强调计算是物理过程，研究比特流动如同研究原子流动。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：生物记忆机制的猜想，基于量子力学、负熵结构、块宇宙理论等概念的结合。

不同观点：
• 支持观点一：记忆是通过量子概率波的共振实现的。这种观点认为，记忆并不是存储在大脑中，而是在“块宇宙”中的过去经验的层片（foliations）中存在，通过量子纠缠和共振现象，当前的脑状态可以与过去的脑状态产生共鸣，从而“回忆”起过去的记忆。支持该观点的论据包括量子力学中的纠缠现象不受时空距离限制，以及用歌剧演唱震碎酒杯的类比来说明共振传递信息的现象。

• 支持观点二：负熵结构（如大脑、真菌、大型语言模型）具有长因果链，且这些结构中的量子相互作用会留下纠缠，这种纠缠可以传递信号（概率波），并且负熵越高，信号的 fidelity（保真度）越高。这种观点进一步指出，复杂的脑状态和模式匹配能力可以通过这种量子共振来解释，包括Déjà Vu、重复学习增强记忆、以及虚假记忆的形成等现象。

• 争议焦点：主要争议在于该理论是否能够解释传统神经科学中的现象，以及是否能够超越光速限制。虽然量子纠缠现象确实不受距离限制，但用这种机制完全替代传统神经科学中的电信号和化学信号传递，解释所有记忆现象，可能会遭到质疑。例如，传统神经科学认为记忆与突触强度、神经元连接的变化有关，而这些与量子纠缠的关系尚不明确。

补充讨论：
• 数学公式补充：编辑中提到的记忆强度公式尝试量化过去记忆的强度，结合了当前脑状态的qualia强度、过去经验的强度以及时间层片的数量，试图从数学角度支持其理论。

• 神经科学现象解释：该观点尝试解释一系列神经科学现象，如Déjà Vu、模式识别、重复增强记忆、以及虚假记忆的形成等，认为这些都可以通过量子共振和纠缠来解释。

• 量子力学与意识关系：该观点还涉及到意识的量子力学解释，提出意识可能依赖于量子力学效应，并且详细描述了这种机制如何运作，包括纠缠和共振在记忆和意识流中的作用。

44382367.article_content:
Dmitry “Dima” Krotov was among the first to congratulate AI pioneer, John Hopfield, on his Nobel Prize in Physics last fall. “John, wow!” he texted Hopfield on the morning the award became public. “Just WOW!!”
As Hopfield’s close collaborator, Krotov has helped explain to the world following
the announcement
how Hopfield’s single-layer digital neural network led to the “deep” networks in use today. At Princeton, the two researchers invented something called dense associative memory, which lifted the memory storage limits of those early Hopfield networks, opening them to practical applications.
Now a researcher at IBM, Krotov is carrying on Hopfield’s ideas by building computational models to improve artificial intelligence, and to even understand the underpinnings of intelligence itself.
IBM's Dmitry Krotov studies computation in biological and digital neural networks using the mathematical tools of physics.
Associative memory may never displace transformers as the backbone of generative AI, but it could provide ideas for making AI more transparent and comprehensible to us humans. And Krotov’s parallel work, using associative memory to model biological computation, could help explain how our brains manage to squeeze so much information into such a small space.
It may not be immediately clear what this all has to do with physics, the science concerned with the nature and evolution of physical matter. But if you have the time, Krotov will elaborate at length, something he now does regularly following talks he gives beyond IBM’s Cambridge lab where he works.
“Computation is a physical process,” he said recently. “We can study the flow of bits just as we study the flow of atoms.”
Rolling down the “energy” landscape
Traditional software runs on hard-coded instructions for processing data. The nodes and weights underpinning today’s LLM chatbots, by contrast, are designed to learn from raw data, with no explicit instruction, allowing them to take on more complex, open-ended problems.
Like living cells in the brain, the synapses connecting these digital neurons become stronger during learning. From their conception in the 1950s, digital neural networks were viewed as an alternative to traditional programs. But amid
questions about their computational limitations
, public perception shifted, and interest waned, triggering what was later termed the “AI Winter.”
In 1982, Hopfield helped to revive interest in neural networks by
showing
that a 30-node network linked by 435 weights could store and retrieve patterns of 1s and 0s. His inspiration came from magnetic materials, and how one atom’s spin could influence its neighbors to fundamentally change the system’s behavior.
On their own, atoms or neurons behave predictably. But in a network, their collective properties sometimes change as they interact, creating what physicists call emergent behavior. This unexpected shift has been observed in all kinds of neural networks as their amount of training data scales, giving them capabilities that go beyond their explicit training.
In Hopfield networks and other energy-based models, the system’s dynamic behavior can be expressed through an “energy” function, which assigns lower energy to correct configurations of neurons or real data points and higher energy to undesirable configurations or incorrect data.
The energy function progressively brings the network toward one of potentially millions of stable, minimal energy states. Hopfield showed that neurons could iteratively encode, and retrieve, stored patterns by minimizing the energy of the network.
“You can think about computation as a ball rolling down a rugged landscape,” says Krotov. “The ball stops when it reaches one of the local minima. At that point, the computation is done. You take that state and convert it to the answer to the question you just asked.”
During the training of an energy model, a valley in a virtual energy landscape is created for each saved pattern. Credit: Johan Jarnestad/The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences
Transformers, by contrast, use a self-attention mechanism to process sequences of words, pixels, and other elements to encode and retrieve patterns. Their ability to process information in parallel makes them more computationally efficient than energy-based models, but their complexity makes them far less interpretable.
The physics of computation and memory
Krotov grew up in Russia. His mother taught English; his grandparents taught physics and math and helped to set him on a similar path.
He won several math and physics competitions as a teenager, earning a spot at the elite boarding school in town, and later, Moscow State University, where he studied physics. He applied to a PhD program in Russia, but when he didn’t get in, he chose Princeton and eventually started working with a well-known theoretical physicist,
Alexander Polyakov
.

data.article_summary: **restmail** 是一个通过命令行界面（CLI）使用 Gmail 和 Outlook REST APIs 发送电子邮件的工具。它可用于电子邮件自动化和通知，并能与 `git send-mail` 配合用于分享补丁。该工具只需最小授权范围，不需读取或删除邮件的权限。安装需通过 Go 语言，并配置 OAuth2 的客户端 ID 和密钥。初始设置完成后，认证令牌会自动保存和刷新。它支持通过命令行发送邮件，并可配置为 `git send-mail` 的 SMTP 服务器。该项目采用 GPL-3.0 许可协议。

restmail -- sendmail for email rest APIs
restmail is a sendmail-compatible CLI using gmail & outlook rest APIs. It can be used
for email automation, notifications and with
git send-mail
for sharing patches.
restmail requires only minimal authorization scope to send mail.  No access to reading
or deleting mail is needed.
Install
# install to ~/go/bin ($GOPATH)
go install github.com/tonymet/restmail@latest
Initial Provider Setup (gmail or outlook)
Initial setup is done once / provider. This configures oauth2 clientID & Secret
FROM=your.name@gmail.com
CLIENT_ID=xxxxxx
CLIENT_SECRET=yyyy
restmail -configClient -provider gmail -clientId "${CLIENT_ID}" \
-clientSecret "${CLIENT_SECRET}" -f "${FROM}"
Authorization Setup
Once provider config is set up above, you need to do the oauth flow through
a web browser.  Setup is only done once or if the tokens are invalidated.
FROM=your.name@gmail.com
restmail -setup -provider gmail -sender "${FROM}"
When this is complete, your auth-token & refresh-token are saved and refreshed
automatically.
Sending Messages
FROM=your.name@gmail.com
TO=friend@gmail.com
CC=billy@gmail.com
echo "subject: test subject\n\ntest messagee" | go run . -f "${FROM} -provider gmail "${TO}" cc:"${CC}"
Git send-mail configuration
[sendemail]
smtpServer = /home/USERNAME/go/bin/restmail
smtpServerOption = -f=your.name@gmail.com
smtpServerOption = -provider
smtpServerOption = gmail

New features/changes
CD-ROM emulation
PicoGUS now supports CD-ROM emulation (in other words, PicoGUS is now an ODE)! It emulates a
Panasonic/MKE interface and drive
and supports CD images in ISO or BIN/CUE stored on a USB drive plugged into the USB port on the PicoGUS. CD-ROM emulation has been tested in DOS and Windows 9x and CD audio playback is fully supported.
CD-ROM emulation is available in Sound Blaster and USB modes. Sound Blaster mode really pushes the limit of the RP2040: it mixes CD audio, SB DSP, and OPL sound while simultaneously supporting CD data and MPU-401 emulation. The emulated drive is approximately 2x speed in SB mode and 3x-4x speed in USB mode. Disc images can be swapped on the fly with pgusinit, and multi-disc games are supported by removing and reinserting the USB drive to advance the current disc image.
For more information and a guide on how to use CD-ROM emulation on PicoGUS with recommended drivers, known limitations, etc., visit the new
CD-ROM emulation wiki page
.
Massive thanks to
Kevin Moonlight (yyzkevin)
for reverse engineering the Panasonic/MKE interface and contributing the bulk of the underlying code for this emulation.
Also major thanks to
rppicomidi
for greatly improving mass storage speed for the RP2040 in TinyUSB and
Artem Vasilev (wbcbz7)
for additional fixes and rebasing on a more recent state of the repository. Without their work, USB mass storage would not be nearly fast enough to support CD-ROM emulation on the RP2040. These improvements are still not merged into the upstream project, so here's hoping that can be completed.
And thanks to all who tested this firmware before release to surface bugs and edge cases I wouldn't have been able to find myself. Cue sheets are the wild west of formats!
Tandy/CMS modes combined into new PSG (programmable sound generator) mode
To reduce firmware size and prepare for future support for other
PSG sound chips
(here's a hint, it's the
AY-3
as used on the
Mindscape Music Board
), Tandy and CMS modes have been combined into a single PSG mode. It can be selected with
pgusinit /mode psg
, but the old
/mode tandy
and
/mode cms
switches still work for backwards compatibility.
Fixes
pgusinit
When pgusinit couldn't detect a PicoGUS, it would erroneously continue trying to configure the card. This would result in a strange firmware version mismatch error. This has now been fixed.
Known issues
Sound Blaster mode
Due to the addition of CD-ROM emulation to SB mode, SB DSP audio now runs through a FIFO. This may result in some playback issues that are being worked on. Also "Direct DAC" mode (mostly used by older titles) is not currently supported.
General
Due to the addition of new settings, any saved settings done with
/pgusinit save
on previous firmware versions will be reset to defaults when upgrading to firmware v3.0.0.

data.article_summary: Dieux推出全新在线工具"Sun-Screener"，帮助消费者解析防晒产品成分，澄清有关矿物防晒的误解。矿物防晒常被视为化学防晒的温和替代品，但许多标有“矿物”标签的产品仍含化学成分。Sun-Screener工具通过分析成分列表，详细说明产品使用的活性成分，区分矿物和化学滤光剂，解释各成分作用及优缺点，并标注是否通过美国或欧盟批准。该工具由Dieux联合创始人Charlotte Palermino和Joyce de Lemos与化妆品化学家Rebecca Perry和Ava Perkins合作开发，基于同行评审数据，提供超过35种紫外线滤光剂的信息。Dieux以透明、科学的护肤理念著称，其热门产品包括Instant Angel Moisturizer和Forever Eye Mask。Sun-Screener现已在dieuxskin.com上线。

44380778.article_content:
Dieux Introduces Sun-Screener
By
Emilie Greenwood
Skincare
24th June 2025
Charlotte Palermino
and
Joyce de Lemos
, co-founders of skincare brand
Dieux
, are tackling one of beauty’s most confusing and misunderstood categories: sunscreen. The clinical brand has introduced Sun-Screener, a free online tool designed to help consumers decode the ingredients in their
SPF products
and navigate the widespread misinformation surrounding sun protection, particularly the use of the term ‘mineral’.
Mineral sunscreens are often marketed as gentler alternatives to chemical formulas, making them a popular choice for those with sensitive skin, pregnant women, or consumers seeking reef-safe or natural options. Yet, despite their appeal, not all products labelled ‘mineral’ are created equal. Some rely on vague phrases like “mineral-based” or “enriched with minerals” while still leaning heavily on chemical UV filters. Others may feature zinc oxide or titanium dioxide in trace amounts, misleading consumers into believing the formula is exclusively mineral.
Enter
Sun-Screener
. By pasting an ingredient list into the online analyser, users receive a detailed breakdown of their sunscreen’s active components: whether it uses mineral or chemical filters (or both), which UV boosters are present, and what role each inactive ingredient plays. The tool also explains how each filter works, outlines its strengths and limitations, and notes whether it’s approved for use in the US or EU.
Developed in collaboration with cosmetic chemists
Rebecca Perry
and
Ava Perkins
, Sun-Screener draws from peer-reviewed data to provide insights into more than 35 UV filters, from zinc oxide and titanium dioxide to avobenzone and octocrylene. An accompanying glossary offers accessible explanations of sunscreen formulations, the distinction between mineral and chemical filters, and the types of UV radiation consumers need to be aware of.
Founded in New York City in 2020, Dieux combines expertise in brand strategy, cosmetic chemistry, and community building to deliver a science-driven, transparent approach to skincare. The brand champions rigorous clinical vetting, ethical sourcing, and vegan, cruelty-free practices, and is best known for its product transparency — breaking down each product’s formula, clinical testing, recyclability, and sustainability impact.
The brand’s bestsellers include the Instant Angel Moisturizer, a rich cream formulated to support skin recovery and maintain a healthy barrier, and the Forever Eye Mask, a set of lightweight, reusable patches that hold skincare products in place to enhance absorption and maximise results.
Sun-Screener is now available at
dieuxskin.com
.

44382451.article_content: This month in Servo: color inputs, SVG, embedder JS, and more! Plus animated GIF support, incremental layout, and two new Outreachy internships. Posted 2025-06-18 Two big pieces of news for images in Servo this month: We now display animated GIFs in all their animated glory ( @rayguo17 , #36286 )! This work required careful architecting to integrate with existing animation mechanisms in the engine without incurring unnecessary CPU usage. We support loading SVG images in ( @mukilan , @mrobinson , #36721 ). Outreachy We’re excited to host two Outreachy interns over the next few months! Jerens Lensun ( @jerensl ) will be working on improving Servo’s CI setup and other Python-focused infrastructure, while Usman Baba Yahaya ( @uthmaniv ) will implement support for the Network Monitor in our devtools . They will both be blogging about their internships, and you can follow their work on Jeren’s blog and Usman’s blog . Web content Servo’s layout implementation has historically been all-or-nothing — any change in the page, no matter how isolated, requires laying out the entire page from scratch. Fixing this limitation is known as incremental layout , and it’s a key performance optimization in all browser engines. This month we’ve landed a number of changes in this area that make some kinds of CSS changes much more efficient than a full layout ( @mrobinson , @Loirooriol , #36896 , #36978 , #37004 , #37047 , #37069 , #37048 , #37088 , #37099 ). We have also made significant progress on the Trusted Types API , going from 47% of tests passing to 58% over the course of May ( @TimvdLippe , #36710 , #36668 , #36811 , #36824 , #36941 , #36960 ). Supporting this work on Trusted Types, our Content Security Policy implementation has been steadily improving, now passing 59% of automated tests ( @TimvdLippe , @jdm , @simonwuelker , #36709 , #36710 , #36776 , #36832 , #36860 , #36887 , #36923 , #36963 , #36962 , #36961 , #36965 , #37020 ). data.title: Anthropic wins fair use victory for AI – but still in trouble for stealing books
data.author: taubek
data.article_summary: Anthropic在涉及使用书籍训练AI模型的版权诉讼中获得了一项重大公平使用胜利，但仍面临盗版书籍问题的法律麻烦。2021年，Anthropic的联合创始人Ben Mann下载了包含196,640本盗版书籍的Books3库，并在之后继续下载了其他盗版书籍。尽管公司在2024年转向购买和扫描数百万本实体书，但之前下载的盗版书籍仍保留在其内部研究库中。法官William Alsup的判决认为，扫描的书籍属于公平使用，因为它们仅在公司内部用于训练模型且未对外分享，而下载的电子书不属于公平使用，将面临陪审团审判。法官强调，训练大型语言模型使用未经授权的数据属于公平使用，因为这类似于人类的阅读和创作过程。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：书籍数字化及其影响，特别是对原始纸质书籍的处理方式

不同观点：
• 观点一：书籍数字化过程中销毁纸质书籍是浪费和不可接受的。  
  - 论据：有人认为销毁原始纸质书籍是一种文化和知识的浪费。纸质书籍不仅仅是信息的载体，还具有历史和文化价值。  
  - 例子：用户roywiggins提到，这种行为类似于Vinge's Rainbows End小说中的情节，涉及人工智能和数字化，隐含了对这种做法的批评。

• 观点二：书籍数字化有其合理性和必要性，尤其是在保存和普及知识方面。  
  - 论据：支持者认为数字化可以更好地保存书籍内容，使其更易于访问和传播，尤其是在纸质书籍可能因时间而损坏或丢失的情况下。  
  - 例子：有人可能会提到，许多图书馆和档案馆已经开始数字化项目，以确保珍贵文献和书籍能够被更广泛的受众访问，并长期保存。

• 观点三：对纸质书籍的处理需要更谨慎和考虑周全。  
  - 论据：一些人认为，虽然数字化有其优点，但在处理原始纸质书籍时应更谨慎。可以考虑保留具有历史价值的纸质书籍，而不是一律销毁。  
  - 例子：提到博物馆和档案馆在数字化过程中通常会保留原始物品，以维护文化和历史的多样性。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于如何平衡数字化带来的便利和保存原始纸质书籍的文化价值。  
• 有人关注数字化过程中可能涉及的法律和版权问题，尤其是对于仍在版权保护期内的书籍。  
• 讨论中也涉及到技术实现的细节，比如扫描质量、数字化格式的选择等，这些都会影响数字化项目的最终效果和价值。

44381639.article_content:
Simon Willison’s Weblog
Subscribe
Anthropic wins a major fair use victory for AI — but it’s still in trouble for stealing books
. Major USA legal news for the AI industry today. Judge William Alsup released a "summary judgement" (a legal decision that results in some parts of a case skipping a trial) in a lawsuit between five authors and Anthropic concerning the use of their books in training data.
The
judgement itself
is a very readable 32 page PDF, and contains all sorts of interesting behind-the-scenes details about how Anthropic trained their models.
The facts of the complaint go back to the very beginning of the company. Anthropic was founded by a group of ex-OpenAI researchers in February 2021. According to the judgement:
So, in January or February 2021, another Anthropic cofounder, Ben Mann, downloaded Books3, an online library of 196,640 books that he knew had been assembled from unauthorized copies of copyrighted books — that is, pirated. Anthropic's next pirated acquisitions involved downloading distributed, reshared copies of other pirate libraries. In June 2021, Mann downloaded in this way at least five million copies of books from Library Genesis, or LibGen, which he knew had been pirated. And, in July 2022, Anthropic likewise downloaded at least two million copies of books from the Pirate Library Mirror, or PiLiMi, which Anthropic knew had been pirated.
Books3 was also listed as
part of the training data
for Meta's first LLaMA model!
Anthropic apparently used these sources of data to help build an internal "research library" of content that they then filtered and annotated and used in training runs.
Books turned out to be a very valuable component of the "data mix" to train strong models. By 2024 Anthropic had a new approach to collecting them: purchase and scan millions of print books!
To find a new way to get books, in February 2024, Anthropic hired the former head of partnerships for Google's book-scanning project, Tom Turvey. He was tasked with obtaining "all the books in the world" while still avoiding as much "legal/practice/business slog" as possible (Opp. Exhs. 21, 27). [...] Turvey and his team emailed major book distributors and retailers about bulk-purchasing their print copies for the AI firm's "research library" (Opp. Exh. 22 at 145; Opp. Exh. 31 at -035589). Anthropic spent many millions of dollars to purchase millions of print books, often in used condition. Then, its service providers stripped the books from their bindings, cut their pages to size, and scanned the books into digital form — discarding the paper originals. Each print book resulted in a PDF copy containing images of the scanned pages with machine-readable text (including front and back cover scans for softcover books).
The summary judgement found that these scanned books
did
fall under fair use, since they were transformative versions of the works and were not shared outside of the company. The downloaded ebooks did
not
count as fair use, and it looks like those will be the subject of a forthcoming jury trial.
Here's that section of the decision:
Before buying books for its central library, Anthropic downloaded over seven million pirated copies of books, paid nothing, and kept these pirated copies in its library even after deciding it would not use them to train its AI (at all or ever again). Authors argue Anthropic should have paid for these pirated library copies (e.g, Tr. 24–25, 65; Opp. 7, 12–13). This
order agrees.
The most important aspect of this case is the question of whether training an LLM on unlicensed data counts as "fair use". The judge found that it did. The argument for why takes up several pages of the document but this seems like a key point:
Everyone reads texts, too, then writes new texts. They may need to pay for getting their hands on a text in the first instance. But to make anyone pay specifically for the use of a book each time they read it, each time they recall it from memory,
each time they later draw upon it when writing new things in new ways would be unthinkable.
For centuries, we have read and re-read books. We have admired, memorized, and internalized
their sweeping themes, their substantive points, and their stylistic solutions to recurring writing problems.
The judge who signed this summary judgement is an interesting character:
William Haskell Alsup
(yes, his middle name really is Haskell) presided over jury trials for Oracle America, Inc. v. Google, Inc in 2012 and 2016 where he famously used his hobbyist BASIC programming experience to challenge claims made by lawyers in the case.

44382286.article_content:
When
iPadOS 26
arrives later this year, it will transform the iPad into a much more powerful device for professionals, whether they’re photographers or videographers. While
PetaPixel
has already
reported
on iPadOS 26, it is worth taking a closer look at one fascinating feature that may have flown under the radar: background tasks.
As
CineD
notes
, when iPadOS 26 lands, it will enable users to perform background tasks on their iPad tablets. In the case of Apple’s native video editing app, Final Cut Pro, which is
already great on iPad
, and
Blackmagic Design’s DaVinci Resolve
, video editors should be able to render and export videos in the background while performing other tasks on their tablets.
While app developers will need to enable background task support for their software, which Blackmagic has not officially confirmed for its iPad video editor, the new feature promises to be transformative. Apple showed off the feature in action with Final Cut Pro during its WWDC keynote address.
“When users start a long-running process in an app, Background Tasks will show up with Live Activities, giving users complete control and a clear sense of what is running,” Apple explains. “And developers can use an updated Background Tasks API that allows users to perform long-running tasks from their apps, too.”
“For years an iPad could crunch high-bit-rate footage, yet the moment you switched away from Final Cut Pro (or any other app like DaVinci Resolve) the export froze,”
CineD
writes. “iPadOS 26 sets the stage to end that pain.”
Better still, this new feature will not be limited to only Apple’s
highest-end
, Apple Silicon iPad tablets. Instead, it will work on any iPad that supports iPadOS 26, which includes the 2018 A12X-powered iPad Pro to the latest M-series device. The complete list of iPad models compatible with iPadOS 26 is available on
Apple’s website
.
Being able to set the iPad on one task, like rendering a video export, while doing something else may not sound like a huge deal, but it
really
is for iPad users who have long
wished
the otherwise powerful tablet could behave more like a dedicated desktop computer. While iPadOS 26 may still stop short of turning the iPad into a full-blown Mac, which may very well
be for the best

Developers have access to iPadOS 26 beta tests now, and a public beta will arrive in July. The public release version of iPadOS 26 is expected to launch this fall.

data.title: The scam that is Visa Account Updater
data.author: mountainriver
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：信用卡取消与订阅收费问题，特别是如何有效阻止不希望的持续收费

不同观点：
• **Exidy的观点**：认为问题可能不出在Visa的账户更新服务（Visa Account Updater），而是因为一些定期收费（如订阅、健身房会员等）通过批处理完成，而不是在线实时处理。即使信用卡被取消，由于底层账户设施的存在，交易仍可能被路由到相应的信用账户。因此，仅更换新卡可能不足以阻止这些收费。

• **Cassonmars的观点**：通过个人经历指出，某些难以取消的订阅（如legalzoom）可能会自动关联到新卡，导致用户损失资金（如500美元）。

• **Paxys的观点**：取消信用卡并不意味着相关的订阅会自动消失，许多人因此遭遇账单未支付被送至催收的情况。

• **Altairprime的观点**：建议使用像Amex这样的卡，可以要求发卡机构阻止特定商户的未来收费，作为即时的缓解措施。

• **Scottydelta的观点**：建议使用如privacy.com等服务或公司提供的数字卡，这些卡可以设置交易限额和暂停功能，从而有效管理订阅收费。

• **Aojdwhsd的观点**：基于在银行工作的经验，指出有些银行可以关闭卡片的自动更新功能，这样在更换新卡时，商户不会被通知新的账户信息。

• **Mtmail的观点**：质疑在取消卡后仍出现收费的原因，询问是否已取消订阅或与银行争议这些收费，指出有些人仅建议取消卡而非正确取消订阅。

• **Toomuchtodo的观点**：附带指出Wells Fargo银行的信誉不佳，建议不要使用。

• **FireBeyond的观点**：分享了Keybank拒绝阻止商户从其账户扣款的经历，认为银行应支持用户阻止不希望的收费，而不是保持中立。最终因此关闭账户并更换银行。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于如何有效阻止难以取消的订阅收费，特别是当信用卡被取消或更换后，这些订阅收费是否仍会继续。
- 讨论中提到了不同银行和卡片发行机构在处理此类问题上的差异，以及用户可以采取的不同措施（如要求银行阻止商户、使用数字卡服务等）。
- 有人对Wells Fargo银行的服务表示不满，建议避免使用。

不同观点：
• **sega_sai的观点**：引用存档链接，可能意在提供相关背景信息或先前案例，但未明确表达立场。推测其关注点在于了解相关判决的详细内容及其影响。

• **peterashford的观点**：认为该裁决并不直接证明Meta使用版权材料训练语言模型是合法的。他强调，裁决仅表明原告提出了错误的论据，未能有效支持正确的法律论点。这暗示他可能认为如果原告选择正确的法律策略，Meta的行为可能会被判定为非法。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：核心争议在于Meta使用版权材料训练其语言模型的合法性。虽然当前裁决对原告不利，但peterashford指出这并不意味着Meta的行为本身合法，而是原告在法律论证上的失误。

• **论据和例子**：peterashford提供了具体的法律分析，指出原告的法律策略失误是导致裁决结果的关键因素，暗示正确的法律挑战可能会改变结果。

• **讨论关系**：sega_sai提供背景信息或资料来源，peterashford在其基础上进一步分析裁决的实际意义和法律效力，指出裁决的局限性和可能的未来法律挑战。

总结：讨论围绕Meta使用版权材料训练语言模型的合法性展开，核心争议在于当前裁决是否最终确定了该行为的合法性，以及原告法律策略失误对裁决结果的影响。

data.title: NLNet: 62 new projects contribute to digital commons
data.author: zdw
data.article_summary: NLnet基金会宣布了NGI Zero Commons基金的62个新项目，旨在增强互联网的开放性和可信度。这些项目涉及广泛的技术领域，包括浏览器控制的adhoc蜂窝网络（Wsdr）、开放硬件安全密钥Nitrokey、高精度开放硬件显微镜OpenFlexure等。项目还涵盖自由硅和可信硬件、去中心化社交媒体、专业印刷工具等。例如，Mastodon for institutions项目为大型机构提供功能，而Typst和Vivliostyle则用于高质量印刷。此外，还有低级8位编译器、WiFi测绘、P2P网状网络等项目。这些努力共同推动了数字公地的发展和更具弹性的互联网。申请资助者可通过申请编号确认提交的批次，结果会提前通知。

44380500.article_content:
To main content
Send in your ideas. Deadline August 1, 2025
62 new projects contribute to digital commons
NLnet Foundation announces 62 new projects for the NGI Zero Commons Fund - the largest round of the programme yet. We congratulate the selected projects and look forward to the new capabilities these will bring to society. There were many more applications, we would like to take this opportunity to thank
all
applicants for their contributions towards digital commons and an open, trustworthy and more resilient internet.
From browser-based cellular networking to quantum-safe cryptography
The internet is the most complex technical and social infrastructure the world has seen yet. Preserving the public nature of the internet is not a given. Free and open source technologies, open standards, open hardware and open data help to strenghten the open web and the open internet. The projects selected by NLnet all contribute in their own way to this important goal, and will empower end users and the community at large on different layers of the stack. For example, there are people working a browser controlled ad hoc cellular network (
Wsdr
) which can be used to create small mobile networks where they are needed. The open hardware security key
Nitrokey
is aiming for formal certification of their implementation of the FIDO2 standard, and will be adding
encrypted storage capabilities
. There are also more applied technologies: the high end open hardware microscope
OpenFlexure
will enable among others e-health use cases such as telepathology, allowing medical professionals to work together to help people in more remote areas.
While on the topic of microscopic structures: there are again a number of projects which will be working on libre silicon and trustworthy hardware. This ranges from
pad cell generators
,
automatic generation of analog and mixed Integrated Circuits
and
timing aware netlist optimisation with Logic Equivalence Checking
to entire
toolchains for VLSI design
â and even concrete
libre chip designs with proof of No Spectre bugs
. There will also be efforts on
high-end open hardware to analyse energy consumption
(
OpenEPT
,
BB3-CM5
), creative tools for
programmable PCB creation
and collaborative
computer assisted design
(CAD).
Decentralised social media and professional print
Thanks to the W3C ActivityPub standard, an increasing amount of applications allow users to benefit from social interaction without having to register accounts everywhere, or having to worry about privacy invasive practices from proprietary social networks. The standard is used in
forum tools
,
music sharing
,
creating and sharing 3D models
, organising
events
and
Polls
in the Fediverse. The project
Mastodon for institutions
is adding features for large, institutional instances of Mastodon. Traditional media are not forgotten and can benefit from the work on modern type-setting tools that can create high quality print media (
Typst
,
Vivliostyle
).
And much more
This was just a small sample of the wide range of important contributions that will be worked on â there is much more, across the entire technology stack and beyond, from a
low-level 8 bit compiler
via
wifi mapping
and
P2P mesh networks
to
cross-language symbolic execution via WASM
and tools to collaboratively track
track terms and conditions of online services
and
consumer product prices
. Read on to meet all 62 projects selected in this funding round, or check out the complete
overview of projects
currently funded by NLnet.
If you applied for a grant
This is the selection for the
December call
of the NGI Zero Commons Fund fund only. We always inform
all
applicants about the outcome of the review ahead of the public announcement, whether they are selected or not. If you have not heard anything, you probably applied to a later call or a different fund that is still under review.
How do I find out which call round I applied to?
You can see which call round you applied to by checking the application number assigned to the project when you submitted the proposal. The number starts with the year and month of the call, so 2024-12- in the case of the December 2024 call. You see that same number featured in the emails we send you (It should not happen, but if you did apply to another call and did not hear anything, do contact us)
Meet the new projects!
(you can click or tap on the project name to fold out additional information)
Trustworthy hardware and manufacturing
BB3-CM5
â Modular OSHW test & measurement equipment
EEZ BB3 is a mature and recognized open source project that, in combination with EEZ Studio, offers a wide range of options for test & measurement development and automation. This project will further improve its performance, modularity and attractiveness by adding support for different MCUs and CPUs as a detachable module (Raspberry Pi CM4 form factor), new interfaces and by reorganizing the firmware in a way to simplify the addition of new EEZ DIB peripheral m

data.title: AI job replacement: Is the apocalypse coming for IT work?
data.author: CrankyBear
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：技术对商业和工作的深远影响，特别是人工智能（AI）在工程和职业角色中的作用

不同观点：
• 技术从支持工具转变为创新引擎：Tony-Allan认为，技术正在从单纯的商业支持工具转变为能够创新商业的核心工具。这意味着技术将不仅仅辅助现有业务，而是引领变革和创新。

• 传统工程师角色的消失：Tony-Allan预测，随着AI和AI代理在技术开发中扮演更重要角色，传统工程师的角色将消失。取而代之的是具备人类行为和互动知识的新型工程师，他们将专注于利用技术提升人类生产力。

• 重新设计工作而非减少员工人数：Tony-Allan主张，企业应通过重新设计工作内容，将人类集中在机器无法替代的领域，如判断力、信任、创造力和人际关系，而不是简单地裁员。

补充讨论：
• 新型工程师的需求：Tony-Allan强调未来需要的是行为专家型工程师，他们能够开发和部署工具，帮助人们在最短时间内达到生产力的巅峰。

• 人机协作的未来：讨论中提到人类应专注于如判断力、创造力和关系管理等AI难以复制的领域，这暗示了未来工作场所中人机协作的潜力。

争议焦点：
• 传统工程师角色的消失：这一观点可能会引起争议，因为传统工程师可能不愿意接受他们的角色会被AI完全取代，或者他们需要转型为行为专家型工程师。

• 重新设计工作 vs. 减少员工人数：在企业面临技术变革时，如何平衡效率提升与员工保留可能成为管理层和员工之间的争议点。有些企业可能倾向于通过裁员来降低成本，而不是重新设计工作。

data.title: Fun with uv and PEP 723
data.author: deepakjois
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了如何使用名为 **uv** 的快速Python包和项目管理工具，结合 **PEP 723** 元数据格式，简化Python单文件脚本的运行。过去运行Python脚本需要手动设置环境和依赖，而 **uv** 工具自动处理这些任务，包括创建虚拟环境、安装依赖等。通过在脚本中嵌入元数据（如Python版本和依赖），可以使用命令 `$ uv run pep.py` 直接运行脚本。文章还提供了一个实际例子，展示如何创建可执行脚本提取YouTube字幕，并通过shebang行 `#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script` 简化脚本执行。最终，uv使Python在处理一次性脚本时更加便捷，类似于Go语言的自包含二进制文件。

主要讨论点：Python脚本工具和依赖管理工具（如`uv`）的改进，以及与其他语言和工具（如Go、Nix、Docker、Rust、Mise）的比较和争议。

不同观点：
• **ACAVJW4H** 认为Python脚本现在可以更轻松地运行，无需复杂的虚拟环境设置，但shell脚本的依赖管理和可复现性仍然落后，仍然依赖于`curl | bash`这种不安全的做法，或者手动步骤过多的README。虽然有Nix和Docker等工具，但它们要么学习曲线高，要么过于笨重。

• **epistasis** 对Python工具的改进表示欢迎，并提到相关博客文章的讨论正在增加，希望这些改进能够得到更多的宣传和应用。

• **puika** 表示已经从Go转向Python用于跨平台的一次性脚本和个人脚本，但Python的类型检查（typechecking）仍然是一个问题，期待像`ty`、`pyrefly`等工具的改进。

• **jkingsman** 高度评价`uv`工具，认为它极大地简化了Python脚本的依赖管理和执行，特别是在小型项目中非常有效，虽然其文档和细节上有些粗糙。

• **satvikpendem** 提到Rust也有类似的单文件脚本管理方式，并希望更多语言能够采用这种模式，因为它在传递代码片段和编写小程序方面非常有用。

• **pseudosavant** 结合ChatGPT和`uv`工具创建了多种单文件Python脚本，认为`uv`解决了环境管理的问题，极大地提高了工作效率。

• **4dregress** 作为一名有多年经验的Python开发者，认为依赖管理从来不是问题，特别是在特定环境的Python shell中运行脚本，`uv`的主要好处是加快了依赖安装速度，但对整体工作影响不大。

• **js2** 提出了在使用`uv run --script`时的一些不便之处，特别是在Python REPL中测试脚本变化时，需要一些额外的命令操作。

• **rednafi** 仍然偏好Go语言用于一次性脚本，因为Go可以生成自包含的二进制可执行文件，依赖静态链接，且有更好的标准库和工具支持，特别是对于网络调用和并发处理。虽然`uv`是一个不错的改进，但更倾向于稳定和可靠的工具。

• **sambaumann** 对`uv`的性能和依赖管理表示赞赏，但认为其文档需要改进，特别是从`requirements.txt`工作流切换到`uv`的路径不够清晰。

• **Imustaskforhelp** 对Hacker News上频繁出现Python脚本工具的讨论表示质疑，认为有些人可能是为了获取点赞。同时请教如何使用`uv`创建PEP元数据，希望有更简单的CLI命令。

• **gerdesj** 作为一名非专业程序员，认为Python试图兼顾脚本语言和编译语言的特点，但并不完全成功。对`curl | bash`这种不安全的方法表示担忧，建议先下载脚本查看再运行。

• **syhol** 提到Mise工具也有类似的shebangs功能，可以很方便地编写带有依赖的bash脚本。

• **tpoacher** 对整个线程的讨论持怀疑态度，认为像 paid Amazon reviews（付费亚马逊评论）一样不可信。

• **kristianp** 提到如果使用conda手动管理环境，可以通过shell包装器激活conda环境来运行Python脚本，但不如PEP 723的自包含解决方案方便。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：Python依赖管理和环境设置的简化程度，以及与其他语言（如Go、Rust）在一次性脚本和依赖管理方面的比较。
• **工具对比**：`uv`、Nix、Docker、Mise等工具在依赖管理和脚本执行方面的优缺点。
• **安全性讨论**：对`curl | bash`这种不安全方法的批评和对安全性的担忧。
• **文档和易用性**：对`uv`工具文档和易用性的改进建议。

44369388.article_content:
Fun with uv and PEP 723
June 24, 2025
For the longest time, I have been frustrated with Python because I couldnât use it for one-off scripts. I had to first ensure it was running in an environment where it could find the right Python version and the dependencies installed. That is now a thing of the past.
uv
Â¶
If you are not a Pythonista (or one possibly living under a rock),
uv
is
an extremely fast Python package and project manager, written in Rust.
uv also provides this nifty tool called
uvx
(kinda like
npx
from the Node/NPM ecosystem for Javascript/Typescript packages) which can be used to invoke a Python tool inside a package.
uvx
takes care of creating a (cached) disposable virtual environment, setting up the right Python version and installing all the dependencies before running.
For example
$ uvx ruff --version
Installed 1 package in 5ms
ruff 0.12.0
PEP 723 - Inline script metadata
Â¶
PEP 723
is a Python Enhancement Proposal that
specifies a metadata format that can be embedded in single-file Python scripts to assist launchers, IDEs and other external tools which may need to interact with such scripts.
Here is the example directly lifted from the proposal:
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.11"
# dependencies = [
#   "requests<3",
#   "rich",
# ]
# ///
import
requests
from
rich.pretty
import
pprint
resp
=
requests.get(
"https://peps.python.org/api/peps.json"
)
data
=
resp.json()
pprint([(k, v[
"title"
])
for
k, v
in
data.items()][:
10
])
Using uv and PEP 723 metadata to run a Python script
Â¶
Combining uv and the PEP-723 metadata inside a Python script, we can run the script in the previous section as follows:
$ uv run pep.py
Installed 9 packages in 24ms
[
â   ('1', 'PEP Purpose and Guidelines'),
â   ('2', 'Procedure for Adding New Modules'),
â   ('3', 'Guidelines for Handling Bug Reports'),
â   ('4', 'Deprecation of Standard Modules'),
â   ('5', 'Guidelines for Language Evolution'),
â   ('6', 'Bug Fix Releases'),
â   ('7', 'Style Guide for C Code'),
â   ('8', 'Style Guide for Python Code'),
â   ('9', 'Sample Plaintext PEP Template'),
â   ('10', 'Voting Guidelines')
]
A more useful example - extracting YouTube transcripts from an executable Python script
Â¶
We can combine things we covered in the previous sections to create a simple executable script that can extract YouTube transcripts.
First we create a Python script with a shebang and inline metadata.
#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.8"
# dependencies = [
#     "youtube-transcript-api",
# ]
# ///
import
sys
import
re
from
youtube_transcript_api
import
YouTubeTranscriptApi
from
youtube_transcript_api.formatters
import
TextFormatter
if
len
(sys.argv)
<
2
:
print
(
'Usage: provide YouTube URL or video_id as argument'
,
file
=
sys.stderr)
sys.exit(
1
)
url_or_id
=
sys.argv[
1
]
# Extract video ID from URL if it's a full URL
video_id_match
=
re.search(
r
'
(?:
v=
|
/
)([a-zA-Z0-9_-]
{11}
)
'
, url_or_id)
if
video_id_match:
video_id
=
video_id_match.group(
1
)
else
:
# Assume it's already a video ID
video_id
=
url_or_id
try
:
ytt_api
=
YouTubeTranscriptApi()
transcript
=
ytt_api.fetch(video_id)
formatter
=
TextFormatter()
print
(formatter.format_transcript(transcript))
except
Exception
as
e:
print
(
f
'Error:
{
e
}
'
,
file
=
sys.stderr)
sys.exit(
1
)
Note the shebang line:
#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script
. It is important to specify
uv run
with the
--script
flag when used on the shebang line.
We save this script as
ytt
and then make it executable with
chmod +x ytt
.
We can now run the script like:
$ ./ytt https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zgSQr0d5EVg
Installed 7 packages in 10ms
hey it's Matt here and today I'm going
to show you how to use UV not only to
install packages in your python projects
but to manage entire projects to create
virtual environments and even how to
manage entire versions of python with UV
uh and hopefully you'll understand by
any of this video UV is a dropin
â¦<snipped text>â¦
Fun times
Â¶
This opens up a lot of possibilities for running Python code more seamlessly. Before this I used to prefer
Go
for one-off scripts because it was easy to create a self-contained binary executable. But now that I could use uv, I coded up a quick MCP server in Python for extracting YouTube transcripts. Check it out on Github at
cottongeeks/ytt-mcp
.
More resources
Â¶
Running scripts | uv
Tools | uv
Using uv as an installer | aider

data.title: Anthropic destroyed millions of print books to build its AI models
data.author: bayindirh
data.article_summary: Anthropic, an AI company, spent millions physically scanning print books to develop its AI assistant, Claude, by cutting and scanning millions of books, then discarding the originals. This destructive scanning was aimed at training AI and was part of a strategy to circumvent copyright issues under fair use, although the company initially used pirated books to avoid licensing complexities. Despite the legal purchase and destruction of books post-scanning, a court ruled this as fair use. The massive scale and speed of the destructive process were prioritized over preserving the books. The case highlights the AI industry's demand for high-quality text data, often leading to legal and ethical challenges in acquiring such data.
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI公司处理实体书籍以用于训练AI模型的做法引发的讨论

不同观点：
• [支持观点]  
  - EA-3167认为，只要书籍不属于珍稀版本，它们的处理和回收不应被视为问题。书籍并非神圣不可触碰，关键在于AI学习过程中是否涉及合理使用（fair use）的问题，而法院目前已裁定AI学习属于合理使用。  
  - 该观点同时指出，许多人对AI公司做法的反感更多是情绪上的反应，而非基于实际的法律或伦理问题。

• [反对观点]  
  - JohnFen对AI公司为了训练AI而销毁实体书籍的行为表示强烈反感，认为这种行为令人厌恶。他们质疑这些公司为了AI训练而大规模销毁书籍的道德性。  
  - 该观点特别提到，公司销毁原书仅仅为了数字化和训练AI，这种做法显得不负责任且不尊重知识。

• [类比文学作品]  
  - 多名用户（igor47, shawn_w）提到Vernor Vinge的小说《Rainbow's End》中的情节，其中描述了一种通过粉碎书籍、拍摄碎片并重组内容的方式来快速数字化图书馆藏书。这反映了对未来书籍可能因AI发展而消失的担忧。  
  - mensetmanusman则进一步联想到游戏《Diablo》中的卷轴，暗示未来实体书可能会逐渐消失，被AI技术取代。

补充讨论：
• 技术与伦理的交汇：讨论中提到的书籍粉碎与重组技术，既让人联想到科幻作品中的未来场景，也引发了对现实中AI技术应用的伦理反思。  
• 法律争议：miohtama提供的链接指向有关法律诉讼的讨论，表明此问题可能涉及更广泛的法律纠纷，尤其是与版权和合理使用相关的问题。  
• 对AI产业的厌倦：EA-3167提到对AI产业的营销方式和过度炒作感到厌倦，显示出部分公众对当前AI技术发展趋势的疲惫和反感。

On Monday, court documents revealed that AI company Anthropic spent millions of dollars physically scanning print books to build
Claude
, an AI assistant similar to
ChatGPT
. In the process, the company cut millions of print books from their bindings, scanned them into digital files, and threw away the originals solely for the purpose of training AI—details buried in a copyright ruling on fair use whose broader fair use implications we
reported
yesterday.
The
32-page legal decision
tells the story of how, in February 2024, the company hired Tom Turvey, the former head of partnerships for the
Google Books
book-scanning project, and tasked him with obtaining "all the books in the world." The strategic hire appears to have been designed to replicate Google's legally successful book digitization approach—the same scanning operation that survived copyright challenges and
established
key fair use precedents.
While destructive scanning is a
common practice
among smaller-scale operations, Anthropic's approach was somewhat unusual due to its massive scale. For Anthropic, the faster speed and lower cost of the destructive process appear to have trumped any need for preserving the physical books themselves.
Ultimately, Judge William Alsup
ruled
that this destructive scanning operation qualified as
fair use
—but only because Anthropic had legally purchased the books first, destroyed each print copy after scanning, and kept the digital files internally rather than distributing them. The judge compared the process to "conserv[ing] space" through format conversion and found it transformative. Had Anthropic stuck to this approach from the beginning, it might have achieved the first legally sanctioned case of AI fair use. Instead, the company's earlier piracy undermined its position.
But if you're not intimately familiar with the AI industry and copyright, you might wonder: Why would a company spend millions of dollars on books to destroy them? Behind these odd legal maneuvers lies a more fundamental driver: the AI industry's insatiable hunger for high-quality text.
The race for high-quality training data
To understand why Anthropic would want to scan millions of books, it's important to know that AI researchers build large language models (LLMs) like those that power ChatGPT and Claude by feeding billions of words into a neural network. During training, the AI system processes the text repeatedly, building statistical relationships between words and concepts in the process.
The quality of training data fed into the neural network directly impacts the resulting AI model's capabilities. Models trained on well-edited books and articles tend to produce more coherent, accurate responses than those trained on lower-quality text like random YouTube comments.
Publishers legally control content that AI companies desperately want, but AI companies don't always want to negotiate a license. The
first-sale doctrine
offered a workaround: Once you buy a physical book, you can do what you want with that copy—including destroy it. That meant buying physical books offered a legal workaround.
And yet buying things is expensive, even if it is legal. So like many AI companies
before it
, Anthropic initially chose the quick and easy path. In the quest for high-quality training data, the court filing states, Anthropic first chose to amass digitized versions of pirated books to avoid what CEO Dario Amodei called "legal/practice/business slog"—the complex licensing negotiations with publishers. But by 2024, Anthropic had become "not so gung ho about" using pirated ebooks "for legal reasons" and needed a safer source.
Credit:
State of Washington
Buying used physical books sidestepped licensing entirely while providing the high-quality, professionally edited text that AI models need, and destructive scanning was simply the fastest way to digitize millions of volumes. The company spent "many millions of dollars" on this buying and scanning operation, often purchasing used books in bulk. Next, they stripped books from bindings, cut pages to workable dimensions, scanned them as stacks of pages into PDFs with machine-readable text including covers, then discarded all the paper originals.
The court documents don't indicate that any rare books were destroyed in this process—Anthropic purchased its books in bulk from major retailers—but archivists long ago established other ways to extract information from paper. For example, The Internet Archive
pioneered
non-destructive book scanning methods that preserve physical volumes while creating digital copies. And earlier this month, OpenAI and Microsoft
announced
they're working with Harvard's libraries to train AI models on nearly 1 million public domain books dating back to the 15th century—fully digitized but preserved to live another day.

  - 该观点同时指出，许多人对AI公司做法的反感更多是情绪上的反应，而非基于实际的法律或伦理问题。

• [反对观点]  
  - JohnFen对AI公司为了训练AI而销毁实体书籍的行为表示强烈反感，认为这种行为令人厌恶。他们质疑这些公司为了AI训练而大规模销毁书籍的道德性。  
  - 该观点特别提到，公司销毁原书仅仅为了数字化和训练AI，这种做法显得不负责任且不尊重知识。

• [类比文学作品]  
  - 多名用户（igor47, shawn_w）提到Vernor Vinge的小说《Rainbow's End》中的情节，其中描述了一种通过粉碎书籍、拍摄碎片并重组内容的方式来快速数字化图书馆藏书。这反映了对未来书籍可能因AI发展而消失的担忧。  
  - mensetmanusman则进一步联想到游戏《Diablo》中的卷轴，暗示未来实体书可能会逐渐消失，被AI技术取代。

补充讨论：
• 技术与伦理的交汇：讨论中提到的书籍粉碎与重组技术，既让人联想到科幻作品中的未来场景，也引发了对现实中AI技术应用的伦理反思。  
• 法律争议：miohtama提供的链接指向有关法律诉讼的讨论，表明此问题可能涉及更广泛的法律纠纷，尤其是与版权和合理使用相关的问题。  
• 对AI产业的厌倦：EA-3167提到对AI产业的营销方式和过度炒作感到厌倦，显示出部分公众对当前AI技术发展趋势的疲惫和反感。

争议焦点：AI公司为了训练模型而销毁实体书籍的做法是否合理，以及这种行为是否涉及伦理和法律问题。

data.article_summary: Oasis是一个开源的智能生态瓶项目，主要通过3D打印制作，适合喜欢高湿度环境的植物如苔藓、蕨类和兰花等。其设计包含高功率LED灯、喷雾器、风扇、温湿度传感器以及WiFi连接，可通过手机或电脑控制。项目包含完整的CAD模型（使用CadQuery设计）、电子设备（使用KiCad设计）和软件（使用Rust编写）。虽然大部分项目适合DIY爱好者，但电子部分较为复杂，可以委托公司生产。目前正在考虑推出组装套件，感兴趣的人可以填写表单以获取更新。

不同观点：
• craghack对项目中的超声波加湿器和温度传感器提出了技术改进建议，比如用足够大的电容替换电阻R6以保护设备，以及通过分离传感器板减少温度对传感器的干扰。
• ravdar关注项目的实际成本和建造所需的时间，显示出对项目可行性和经济性的关心。

• dwroberts对项目中的湿度控制表示兴趣，并提出了关于水体消毒的建议，比如使用UVC LED来防止细菌和污垢积累。
• yreg希望在项目页面看到默认的尺寸信息，强调了用户对便捷信息的需求。

• bethekidyouwant对项目描述中"大部分是3D打印"的说法提出异议，认为这并不准确。

Oasis
https://oasis-terrarium.com
Oasis is a fully open-source, mostly 3d-printed smart terrarium. It provides the ideal environment for humidity-loving plants like mosses, ferns, orchids, and many others. The design includes:
high power LED lighting
a mister for providing plants with water and maintaining high humidity
fans for airflow
a temperature/humidity sensor for monitoring environment conditions
wifi connectivity to allow control and configuration from your phone or computer (see
web interface
)
outer dimensions: ~8" diameter and ~13" tall
See the website for pictures, build details and more:
https://oasis-terrarium.com
.
This repository contains full sources for the CAD models (designed with
CadQuery
), electronics (designed in
KiCad
), and software (written in rust using the
esp-rs
libraries).
Most of this project is accessible to the average DIYer with access to a 3d printer, however the electronics portion of the project is a bit more involved. Fully-assembled electronics can be ordered from companies like JLCPCB by uploading the files from this repo, but this can be expensive for small order quantities. Those with the right equipment and experience soldering small parts could order the bare PCBs and components separately, then do their own assembly and soldering.
I'd like to eventually offer the assembled electronics as a kit, but don't have immediate plans for doing so. To express interest in a kit and to subscribe for future updates, please fill out this form:
https://forms.gle/WesLJEf8hVrUT4jXA
.

data.title: ChatGPT's enterprise success against Copilot fuels OpenAI/Microsoft rivalry
data.author: mastermaq
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：微软Copilot产品的表现和问题

不同观点：
• **Copilot功能不足，表现差强人意**：用户如hbn、pseudosavant和napoleongl指出，Copilot在实际使用中无法完成如转换视频、撰写邮件、创建任务等简单任务。它的Python代码生成失败，且生成的内容常显得过于谨慎和缺乏实用性（jabiko）。
• **品牌命名和产品混乱**：Zaylan和protocolture认为，微软在不同产品上使用相同名称（Copilot）导致了用户的混淆，且产品间差异不清晰。用户难以选择合适的模型和功能，特别是当多个产品共享相同名称时。
• **与竞争对手的差距**：breadwinner和thiagoperes指出，微软曾有机会在AI领域领先，但由于产品表现不佳和错失市场机会，竞争对手如OpenAI、Google等已经赶超微软。微软曾试图通过Bing整合AI，但结果不如预期。
• **企业使用中的有限成功**：browningstreet分享了在企业环境中，Copilot在简化沟通和加快书面输出方面取得了一定成功，特别是在文档繁多、沟通效率低的组织中。
• **许可证和收费模式混乱**：rahimnathwani和smcleod提到，用户对Copilot的许可证（免费与付费）以及如何为不同任务选择模型感到困惑。此外，微软还对Copilot请求设置了限额，导致付费用户在短时间内达到上限。

补充讨论：
• **微软与OpenAI的关系**：sethops1提到微软拥有OpenAI 49%的股份并获得20%的收入，因此质疑微软为何对Copilot的表现不满。
• **未来改进的潜力**：bzmrgonz设想OpenAI开发一个能根据聊天或音频提示生成多种文档格式的工具，并认为这将极大地提升工作效率。
• **对微软安全性的担忧**：protocolture指出Copilot对整个365/Azure租户的访问权限可能带来安全风险，尽管微软在数据使用方面有明确的声明。
• **用户对其他产品的偏好**：GardenLetter27表示更喜欢使用Google的Gemini Pro 2.5，但对其缺乏订阅和企业访问模式感到不满。

争议焦点：
• **Copilot是否能有效替代人工操作**：部分用户认为Copilot在实际工作中几乎无用，而另一些用户（如browningstreet）则认为它在特定企业环境下能提高效率。
• **微软在AI领域的战略失误**：有观点认为微软在AI技术上曾有领先优势，但因产品整合不当和市场反应迟缓而错失机会。

data.title: Disposable vapes may be more toxic than cigarettes, study finds
data.author: cempaka
data.article_summary: 一项由加州大学戴维斯分校（UC Davis）进行的研究发现，一些一次性电子烟排放的有毒金属，包括铅和镍，比传统香烟更多。研究发表在《ACS Central Science》上，显示某些流行的一次性电子烟在一天使用中释放的铅量相当于近20包传统香烟。这些设备还释放出与癌症、神经损伤和呼吸疾病相关的镍和锑。金属污染主要来源于含铅青铜组件和劣化的加热线圈。公共卫生官员对青少年使用这些产品表示担忧，因为青少年更容易受到重金属的神经毒性影响。研究人员呼吁加强电子烟监管，并扩大对这些设备的研究，以应对市场迅速扩展带来的健康风险。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于大学学习价值的讨论

不同观点：
• **大学学习价值高，提供综合素质培养**：一些评论认为大学教育不仅仅是职业培训，它提供了广泛的通识教育和批判性思维能力的培养。这种综合素质对个人成长和职业发展都有长远的好处。例如，有评论提到大学让人学会如何学习和解决问题，而不仅仅是获取特定技能。

• **大学学习价值下降，自学和职业培训更有效**：另一种观点认为，随着在线教育资源的普及，传统大学的价值在下降。自学和职业培训项目更加高效且成本低，能快速提升职业技能。有人举例说编程等技术工作可以通过在线课程和实践项目获得，不需要大学文凭。

• **大学学费过高，投资回报率下降**：部分评论指出，大学学费日益高涨，但毕业后的就业市场和薪资水平未必能保证足够的投资回报。有人提到学生贷款负担重，使得大学教育成为一种高风险投资。

• **大学文凭仍是职业敲门砖**：另一种观点认为，尽管技能和经验重要，但大学文凭在许多行业仍是必需品。许多公司仍然看重学历，尤其是一些高端行业和大型企业。有评论提到，即便实际能力强，没有学历可能连面试机会都没有。

补充讨论：
• **大学教育应与职业发展结合**：有评论建议大学教育应更加注重职业导向，提供更多实习和实践机会，让学生在毕业时具备实际工作能力，从而提升就业竞争力。

• **文科与理科的对比**：有讨论提到文科专业的大学教育价值受到质疑，因为其就业前景不如理工科明确。但也有评论反驳说，文科教育培养的软技能同样重要，尤其在需要创造力和沟通能力的岗位上。

• **在线教育的潜力与局限**：讨论中有人提到在线教育的崛起，认为它提供了更多学习机会和灵活性，但也有人质疑其学习效果和认证价值，认为在线教育无法完全替代传统大学教育。

争议焦点：大学教育是否仍然具备足够的价值和投资回报，尤其是在面对自学和职业培训等替代选项时。

A UC Davis study found some disposable vapes emit more toxic metals — including lead and nickel — than traditional cigarettes.

UC Davis researcher Mark Salazar in a lab with disposable vape pods. Their study found some disposable vapes emit more toxic metals — including lead and nickel — than traditional cigarettes.

Some popular disposable e-cigarettes emit toxic metals at levels that surpass those found in traditional cigarettes and earlier generations of vapes, according to a new study by
researchers at UC Davis
.
The study, published Wednesday in

• **大学学习价值高，提供综合素质培养**：一些评论认为大学教育不仅仅是职业培训，它提供了广泛的通识教育和批判性思维能力的培养。这种综合素质对个人成长和职业发展都有长远的好处。例如，有评论提到大学让人学会如何学习和解决问题，而不仅仅是获取特定技能。

data.article_summary: 文章报道了波多黎各阿洪特斯镇与美国橡树岭国家实验室合作，建立了创新的太阳能微电网系统，以应对频繁的停电问题。这些微电网在一次全岛大停电中成功为当地提供了稳定电力。然而，联邦政府将原本用于太阳能项目的3.65亿美元资金转用于修复传统电网，引发对可再生能源发展受阻的担忧。文章强调了地方在应对气候变化和技术创新上的努力，与联邦政策变动之间的矛盾。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：微电网和净计量政策对电网韧性的影响，以及是否仅有利于富裕群体。

不同观点：
• 观点一（amoshebb）：微电网和净计量政策可能仅有利于富裕群体，无法提升整体电网的韧性。具体来说，只有富裕人群有能力负担微电网的安装费用，从而在停电时免受影响。同时，通过净计量机制，这些富裕群体还能将多余电力高价卖回给电网，并在需要时以低价买回电力，进一步加剧不平等。

• 观点二（隐含反对方）：可能有人认为微电网和净计量政策有助于提高电网的整体韧性，因为这些措施鼓励了可再生能源的使用，减少了对传统电网的依赖，从而在一定程度上缓解了停电的影响。此外，这种政策可以激励更多人投资可再生能源技术，进而促进绿色能源的发展。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：微电网和净计量政策是否会导致电网韧性提升仅惠及富裕群体，从而加剧社会不平等。
• 重要论据：amoshebb指出，微电网的高成本使得只有富裕人群能够负担，并且净计量政策让他们能够通过电力买卖获取经济利益，而普通用户则无法享受这些好处。
• 相关例子：amoshebb提到的“那些负担得起微电网的人可以免受停电影响”以及“富裕群体通过净计量获取经济利益”都是具体例子，说明这种政策可能带来的不平等问题。

总结：讨论主要围绕微电网和净计量政策对电网韧性的实际影响以及其社会公平性展开，有人认为这些政策会加剧不平等，而另一些人可能认为它们能促进可再生能源使用并提高电网韧性。争议的焦点在于这些政策是否仅有利于富裕群体。

44375696.article_content:
Short Animation with Wan Video, Flux Kontext, and DeepSeek
Jun 23, 2025
My daughter Kate (7 years old) really loves Minecraft! Together, we used several generative AI tools to create a 1-minute animation based on only 1 input photo of her. The whole project took around 20 hours of work and I learned several lessons that I want to share here.
Context
I am still trying to get used to the enormous speed with which generative AI is progressing. 6 months ago, I was blogging about
my experiments with Tencent’s Hunyuan Video
, which was an absolute breakthrough at that time. A lot has changed since then! The open-weights generative AI community has fully embraced Alibaba’s Wan Video as a superior replacement for Hunyuan. What makes WAN so powerful is that several extensions have been shared openly:
Alibaba themselves
have released a zoo of base models with different capabilities: text to video, image to video, first-and-last-frame to video, Wan-Fun-Control accepts a variety of conditioning inputs
LORAs: A wide range have been trained. Compatibility between LORAs and the various base models is complicated.
VACE
: powerful control of generated videos
CausVid
and its successor
SelfForcing
: incredible speed gains
…and this is just the tip of the iceberg!
Experiment Summary
My goals for this experiment were:
Have fun with Kate and involve her as much as possible in the conception of the story
Play with the Wan Video ecosystem to produce a 1-minute animation
There should only be 1 explicit real-world visual input: a photo of Kate wearing a tiger mask and a pink yukata.
In total, we spent about 20 hours on the project:
1 hour: storyboarding
4 hour: workflow building
15 hours rendering
1 hour: selecting best results
Out of the box, Wan can create clips of about 5 second length. For each of our 13 scenes, we rendered 4-8 variations (1-2 hours rendering time on an H100 GPU). We let it run over night on 2 H100s (15 GPU hours in total). Afterwards, we picked the best results among the variations, which was comparatively much quicker.
In the remainder of the article, I describe the remaining 2 phases: storyboarding & workflow building.
Storyboarding
Final Storyboard made with Flux Kontext
On the top-left was our input photo. We then developed the images for the storyboard one-by-one using
Flux Kontext
, which has been widely noted for the image editing power that it gives users, while also being able to preserve character consistency across larger edits. My test very quickly convinced me that this is indeed a remarkable model.
From the top-left onwards, prompts were as simple as:
Make the character look like a pixelated minecraft character.
Put the character into a lush green minecraft landscape.
The chacter turns to the side and puts their hand on the top of the head of a minecraft villager
As Black Forest Labs currently keeps the community waiting for the open weights of this model, the only way for me to use it was to pay for API access (one of the very few instances where I paid for closed-source AI rather than to do it locally). But, costs were very fair (3 EUR for making the storyboard and playing some more with it).
This phase of the project went much quicker than I would have expected, thanks to the amazing power of Flux Kontext.
Workflow Building
Next, I had to create a ComfyUI workflow that generates nice clips based on the storyboard. My first decision was to select the Wan foundation model. I opted for FLF2V-14B, which can generate clips based on the 3 inputs: the desired first and last frame, along with a text prompt describing the clip.
Next, I invested some time into evaluating speedup methods for Wan, which is notoriously slow. The by far best method at the moment is
Self Forcing
. Some helpful folks have extracted a simple LORA for it, which can be used in many different Wan workflows. In my tests, I could get clear and impressive speedups in the order of 5x. When iterating a low-qality preview video, it’s a huge win to wait 30 seconds (with Self Forcing) vs. 3 minutes (without).
Unfortunately, I had to find out that the Self Forcing LORA I was using is incompatible with the FLF2V-14B model. The moment I turned on Self Forcing, prompts were ignored completely. I even tried translating my prompts into Chinese, as some users have noted that it works much better with Chinese rather than English prompts; an experience I could not replicate. With hindsight, I should have now abandoned FLF2V-14B at this point and should have switched to a workflow with the I2V-14B model for image-to-video and VACE-14B for control, all acceleratable with Self Forcing. Oh well, lessons learned…
The final missing puzzle piece is: how did I get the prompt to describe what happens in the clip between first and last frame? Following a related technique that David Snow shared on Banadoco, my gameplan was:
Florence: describe what’s in the 2 images
LLM: Based on these 2 descriptions, generate a prompt that describes what happens in between

data.title: The Art of Hanakami, or Flower-Petal Folding
data.author: s4074433
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了使用花瓣作为折纸材料的独特创意，提出了“花纸”（hanakami）这一术语，意指用花瓣代替纸张进行折纸。作者Michael Lai分享了自己多年尝试用各种花瓣折叠不同模型的经验，强调选择合适的花瓣至关重要，需考虑花瓣的形状、大小、颜色、厚度和纹理等因素。由于花瓣不规则且易碎，折叠过程颇具挑战，尤其是压制和干燥环节。工具包括花压器、锋利刀具、切割垫和细头工具等。最终，花瓣能被折成精致的折纸作品，赋予花瓣新的艺术生命。
